notes: §E.5: collinear overlaps are merged into a minimal non-overlapping set, the older ID stays on the longest piece; conflicting thickness/height/material -> reject.

These cases check only what the spec fixes for certain: exact coverage, no overlap (totalLength equals the covered length), old ID survives, and the reject rule. How many pieces the line is cut into is left to the implementation.

cases.description: New wall overlaps the last 25 % of an existing wall, same properties.
arithmetic: Union of [0,4000] and [3000,7000] = [0,7000] = 7000 mm. Without merging, total length would be 4000 + 4000 = 8000 (1000 counted twice); required total = 7000.

cases.description: New wall lies completely inside the existing wall, same properties.
arithmetic: [1000,3000] is inside [0,4000]; union stays [0,4000] = 4000 mm. Accept (no change in coverage) or reject are both fine, but there must never be 6000 mm of wall on the line.

cases.description: Exact duplicate (100 % overlap, same direction, same properties).
arithmetic: Merging a duplicate gives back exactly w1 (I3: no two walls share both endpoints). Either 'accepted with no change' or 'rejected' is allowed; in both cases the canonical model equals the input.

cases.description: Exact duplicate drawn in the opposite direction.
arithmetic: Same segment as w1 with a and b swapped; I3 forbids a second wall on j1-j2. w1 keeps its a = j1, b = j2 direction (its openings and left/right materials depend on it).

cases.description: Overlapping wall with a DIFFERENT thickness: conflicting properties -> rejected.
arithmetic: Overlap [3000,4000] would need to be both 200 mm and 100 mm thick -> conflict -> reject (§E.5).
